servo: shorten interface availablility timeout Change the timeout to 5 seconds instead of one minute, so servod isn't unusable for such a long time. If someone accidentally tries to access a cr50 control while servod is disconnected, servod shouldn't become unusable for one minute. 5 seconds should be long enough. The servod wait is just supposed to wait for a device that quickly recovers not a device that is permanently disconnected. Also the watchdog dies before 60 seconds. By the time servod stops waiting the watchdog would have killed it, so 60 seconds is way too long. For wide band speech mode using voice_transparent settings, user space wants to know the value of packet status flag for packet loss concealment. Verified the erroneous data reporting is working fine by flagging lost/partial data. hci: Choose legacy advertising over extended advertising commands. Bluetooth 5.0 (Vol 2, Part E, section 3.1.1) disallows mixing of legacy and extended advertising commands. However, there is no command to explicitly choose which mode (legacy or extended) the host wants to use, but rather the first advertising command will determine whether legacy or extended advertising commands will be allowed for the rest of the controller's lifetime (until Reset). So we call an arbitrary read-only legacy advertising command very early to tell the controller that we want to use the legacy advertising commands instead of extended advertising commands. Without specifying legacy vs extended commands very early, we might hit an unexpected Command Disallowed later on. For example, LE Set Scan Parameters hits Command Disallowed error on Thunder Peak. BUG=chromium:982443 TEST=Manual scanning test on atlas (Thunder Peak). Change-Id: I1ddf22230260e73d646f3d0b1bc5d6f91c822a61 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1677728 Tested-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org>

CRAS: bt_device - Better handle BT audio profile drop This change fixes two things: (1) If BT headset connected, but not able to connect HFP/HSP until timeout, it shall eventually disconnect. (2) If BT headset connected and in use, then A2DP disconnects for some reason, the headset shall disconnect instead of fallback to use HFP/HSP. This change adds cras_bt_device_notify_profile_dropped() as a more generic function to handle unexpected profile drop, by scheduling a full suspend of BT device. We used to rely on the event when HFP AG is dropped and destroyed to send disconnect message to bluetoothd, to make sure the device state changed back to 'disconnected'. However this logic had a bug that if a headset never established an HFP AG, it could miss the disconnect message and leaving BT UI showing the headset still connected. BUG=chromium:755242, b:133790771 TEST=Use unittest to verify. What this change fixes is just difficult to reproduce. Change-Id: Ia7b7606bbb9dfb5cc704a859de143c66cd03829e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1683754 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: bluetooth: Enable filter duplicates field for passive scan This sets the filter duplicates field in LE Set Scan Enabled command to enabled for passive scanning. By enabling the field, the advertisement reports from the same address would be sent to the host once per passive scan cycle. However, since the buffer to keep the seen address is limited (e.g. the size of buffer is 50 for Intel controllers), the host will still be interrupted by any advertisement report with new addresses beyond the size of the buffer. BUG=b:128319712 TEST=(1) Pair and connect Microsoft BluetoothMouse3600 LE mouse from Bluetooth setting page. ml: Get memory usage from proc/[pid]/status The previous code parses /proc/[pid]/totmaps to obtain the memory usage, but this is deprecated and has been removed upstream (crbug.com/979781). In the modification, we instead parse the /proc/[pid]/status and use VmRSS+VmSwap as the memory usage. The new method does not use the hand-coded indices so the result should be more robust. This should be fine because it is the relative sizes of the numbers that matter, rather the absolute values. cros-kernel2.eclass: Add support for generating compile_commands.json Recent kernels allow to generate a 'compilation database' with the compiler flags for each compilation unit. Other programs like LLVM tools or IDEs may use this information for analyzing C source code. Since Chrome OS kernels are built inside the chroot the default compilation DB 'compile_commands_chroot.json' contains chroot paths, which are meaningless for tools running outside the chroot. Also generate a version of the compilation DB with external paths ('compile_commands_no_chroot.json'). The *.json files are installed in /build/${BOARD}/build/kernel. To generate the compilation database the kernel must be built with 'USE=compilation_database'. The feature is only available for kernels that are built with clang (kernels >= 4.4 for most devices).
